title: Implement hard and trails bypass with click free ramps
description:
Extend Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h and Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp (owned earlier by f.1; this is the serialized second write) with hard bypass and trails bypass. Preserve everything f.1 implemented.

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h and .cpp as produced by f.1 (topologies, normalization, mixing, 30 ms wet-path crossfade)
- Source/DSP/FeedbackController.h as produced by f.2 (cross-feedback surface; read only)
- Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h (delay input path; read only)

Required behavior, restated so no external document is needed:
- Hard bypass: fade the wet path out, retain the dry path unchanged, stop delay input, and clear the remaining tail only after the fade transition completes. Do not clear the tail mid-transition.
- Trails bypass: stop new delay input via delayInput = (1 - bypassRamp)*input while the existing tail decays naturally and the dry path continues unchanged.
- Both bypass transitions are 20 ms and must be click-free. Use a dedicated transition ramp member, not an ordinary juce::SmoothedValue.
- The 30 ms routing crossfade from f.1 and the 20 ms bypass ramp are independent transition engines and must not be merged into a single ramp.
- Expose the current delay-input scaling to the caller so PluginProcessor can attenuate voice input during trails bypass, and expose a consumable "tail clear now" signal that becomes true exactly once when a hard-bypass fade completes.

Real-time rules that are binding: no heap allocation, locks, IO, string construction, GUI calls, buffer resizing, or unbounded loops inside the block process function; all ramp state and scratch buffers are allocated in prepare().

Provide at minimum: setBypassMode(BypassMode) with Off, Hard, and Trails states, delayInputGain() returning the current ramped delay-input scale, and consumeTailClearRequest().
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.h declares a bypass mode setter with Off, Hard, and Trails states, a delay-input gain accessor, and a consumable tail-clear request accessor
Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp implements trails bypass as delayInput = (1 - bypassRamp)*input while leaving the dry path unmodified
Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp implements hard bypass as a wet-path fade out that retains dry and only signals tail clearing after the transition completes
Source/DSP/RoutingEngine.cpp uses a 20 ms dedicated bypass ramp that is a separate member from the 30 ms routing crossfade ramp
The topologies, wet normalization N = sqrt(max(1, l_A*l_A + l_B*l_B)), and Insert/Send mixing from task f.1 remain present and unmodified in behavior
The RoutingEngine block process function contains no new/delete, malloc, buffer resize, juce::String construction, or lock acquisition, and does not clear large delay buffers inline
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/FeedbackController.h, Source/DSP/FeedbackController.cpp, Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.h, or Source/DSP/SafetyProcessor.cpp
modify Source/DSP/DelayVoice.h, Source/DSP/DelayVoice.cpp, Source/PluginProcessor.h, or Source/PluginProcessor.cpp
remove or rewrite the topology, normalization, or mixing behavior implemented by task f.1
merge the 20 ms bypass ramp and the 30 ms routing crossfade into one transition engine
attenuate or alter the dry path during trails bypass

allowed: choose the internal bypass ramp representation and member names
choose whether the bypass ramp is per-sample or per-block interpolated, provided it is click-free
forbidden: introduce a new transition or automation abstraction
change the RoutingEngine process signature established by f.1 in a way that breaks existing callers
clear delay buffers from inside RoutingEngine
defer click-free behavior to the integration task
